mo_pontoon_wall.blurb: Pontoon Wall is a limestone sport wall within the Trapper's Camp group of riverside bluffs outside Osceola, in west-central Missouri. It holds 19 routes, most of them bolted and a handful on gear, and it is regarded as the cleanest, steepest stone in the area, running from vertical to overhanging with pockets and rails and a big cave at either end. The grades start around 5.7 but pile up between 5.10 and 5.12, so this is a wall for climbers already comfortable on steep, pocketed lines rather than a first-timer's crag. From the main trail down, walk north beyond the first wall and a brushy gully to reach it. Check every anchor before trusting it.

mo_e_picasso_wall.blurb: Picasso Wall is a sport face of about 60 feet on the north side of Robinson Bluff, a dolomite cliff above the Big River near Tiff in eastern Missouri. All 18 routes are bolted. A few easy 5.7 and 5.8 lines sit alongside a small group of 5.10s, then the numbers climb steadily: the largest share is 5.12, with a single 5.13 at the top end. The wall is multicolored and rust-toned, with crystal-lined pockets; the gentler lines follow deep pockets with fun movement, while the harder ones tackle a bulging roof, and many of those carry permanent draws. Climbs below the roof are mostly 5.9 or easier, making it a good place to warm up before a hard lead.

mo_bluff_two.blurb: Bluff Two is the next bluff north of Bluff One at Scheuler's Ferry, a steep sport destination above the Osage River in central Missouri. It has 19 routes, nearly all bolted with a single trad line. Compared with its busier neighbor, the grade range is wider: a couple of easy 5.6 and 5.7 climbs, a good handful of 5.8s and 5.9s, a solid block of 5.10s, and a few 5.12s at the upper end. Routes at the ferry generally run 40 to 70 feet, so one rope and a set of quickdraws handle most of them. Go past the far end of Bluff One into a broad wooded draw, stay level, and traverse to the bluff's south end.

mo_bluff_one_dihedral_area.blurb: The Dihedral Area is the main section of Bluff One at Scheuler's Ferry, on the Osage River in central Missouri. Of its 19 routes nearly every one is bolted; the exception is a gear line up the corner that gives the area its name, a right-facing dihedral under a big roof amid steep faces. The climbing leans hard. One easy 5.8 and a few 5.9s and 5.10s make up the lower end, while 5.11 is the biggest group and a handful of 5.12s finish the range. Climbs here run roughly 40 to 70 feet, so a single rope, quickdraws and a light rack are all that most people need. The route in is a steep hike beyond the Amphitheater section, along the face.
